deadline.value: Final PhD deadline January 8, 2027; December 1, 2026 is the application-fee-waiver deadline (waivers for U.S.-school students and select international institutions).
deadline.quote: December 1, 2026 Fee waiver* deadline for Ph.D. applicants for Fall 2027 admission. January 8, 2027 Final Ph.D. application deadline for Fall 2027 admission.

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not required and are not used to evaluate PhD applications.
gre_general.quote: GRE scores are not required and will not be used to evaluate applications to the Biomedical Engineering graduate program

ielts_min.value: School of Engineering minimum: TOEFL 89, IELTS 7.0.
ielts_min.quote: proficiency in English must be shown by a minimum score of 89 on the TOEFL, 7.0 on the IELTS test

supervisor.value: Applicants should name the faculty they want to work with in the personal statement.
supervisor.quote: Please make sure to identify faculty you are interested in working with and list them in your Personal Statement.

funding.value: PhD students supported as teaching or research assistants typically get a stipend, health insurance and tuition support; admission is limited by funding and lab positions.
funding.quote: PhD students in our program that are supported as either a teaching assistant or research assistant typically receive a stipend, coverage of health insurance, and tuition support. | Admission to the program is competitive and limited by financial support and available positions in laboratories.

entry_route.value: Applicants should hold a bachelor's degree in engineering or science with some preparation in biology, math and physics; a master's is not required.
entry_route.quote: Applicants for study in biomedical engineering should have a bachelor's degree in engineering or science

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: The BME page still carries an older TOEFL 100 line; the School of Engineering page (TOEFL 89, IELTS 7.0) was used.
